entities.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
entities.desc: YANKEE BLUE is the allegation that the US Air Force ran a fake UFO reverse-engineering programme on its own personnel — briefing officers in classified units into believing they had been read on to a recovery effort, using fabricated material, as a counterintelligence or hazing exercise. If documented it would be the strongest single item in the coverup strand, because it is the government generating false UAP belief inside its own ranks. It is not documented. A full-text search of the released AARO Historical Record Report Volume I (63 pp., March 2024) finds no occurrence of the term, and it appears in none of the FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 consolidated annual reports — which corrects a widely repeated claim, including one this board previously made, that AARO conceded the programme in Volume I. Two FOIA cases have returned negative: OSD case 25-F-3514 (September 2025) reported no responsive records after searches of the electronic and paper holdings, and AFOSI case 2025-06002-F reported no investigative reports, summaries or closure memoranda. On 1 October 2025 Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough stated she could not confirm the alleged memorandum. The Department reportedly reopened the search in December 2025 with no published result. The programme is retained on the board at Tier B with the allegation graded Tier 3 and the negative FOIA findings graded Tier 1. A negative primary finding is itself a documented fact and belongs on a board about concealment — but it is a finding about the absence of a record, not a record.

entities.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
entities.sub: Division M (Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024) of S. 2226 as passed by the Senate, 27 Jul 2023; the same text is Sec. 1104 of S. 2103 as reported by SSCI, 22 Jun 2023. Turn-in mandate STRIPPED in conference; enacted as Sec. 7343, Div. G, P.L. 118-31 — a funding limitation only.

claims.text: The turn-in provision is Sec. 1102 of Division M of S. 2226 as passed by the Senate on 27 July 2023. The Division M table of contents reads 'TITLE XI--OTHER MATTERS Sec. 1101. Modification of reporting requirement for All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office. Sec. 1102. Funding limitations relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.' The same text appears as Sec. 1104 of S. 2103 as reported by SSCI on 22 June 2023; both citations are correct, to different vehicles.

The turn-in mandate did not survive conference. Enacted Sec. 7343 of Division G, P.L. 118-31 contains only (a) definitions, (b) a funding limitation and (c) an IR&D limitation. The phrases 'non-earth origin', 'exotic', 'in their possession' and the 60-day deadline appear nowhere in the enacted text.

Enacted Sec. 7343(b) reads: 'None of the funds authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available by this division may be obligated or expended in support of any activity involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitation unless the Director of National Intelligence has provided the details of the activity to the appropriate committees of Congress and congressional leadership, including for any activities described in a report released by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office in fiscal year 2024.'

The operative text of Sec. 1102 of Division M has NEVER been read verbatim. Six primary vehicles - govinfo HTML and PDF of S.2226es and S.2103rs, SSCI's engrossed PDF, and both formats of the Congressional Record granule - all fail at the same extraction ceiling. The 60-day deadline, the 'non-earth origin or exotic' language and the make-available-to-AARO mandate therefore rest on a secondary source describing REPORTED Sec. 1104, not engrossed Sec. 1102. This is a downgrade of the board's prior confidence, recorded rather than buried. The text was printed in full as SA 1053 at 169 Cong. Rec. S3628-S3642, which is the citation vehicle a future pass should use.
claims.source: 169 Cong. Rec. S3628-S3642 (26 July 2023), granule CREC-2023-07-26-pt1-PgS3627-2

claims.text: The report contradicts itself on satellite flaring. Section IV.C states that AARO resolved 44 UAP-related events as attributable to satellite flaring during the reporting period, while Section I (Executive Summary) and Section VI state that new capability enabled analysts to resolve 238 reported UAP as satellite flaring. Note that a separate figure of 44 UAP reports 'in the space domain' appears at Section III.A and is a different 44.

The annual reporting requirements in subsections (a) and (b) TERMINATED effective 31 December 2021. The statutory note reads: 'For termination, effective Dec. 31, 2021, of provisions in subsecs. (a) and (b) of this section requiring submittal of annual report to Congress, see section 1061 of Pub. L. 114-328, set out as a note under section 111 of this title.' Subsections (c) through (g) survive, and (e)(1) still cross-references the terminated (a) and (b).

The report contains ZERO occurrences of the name 'Wilson' and zero of 'Davis' across all 63 pages including endnotes 1-200. It names no private individuals, referring instead to 'Person 1' and 'the named former CIA official'. It disposes of the reverse-engineering allegations without ever engaging the Wilson-Davis memorandum, a document that sits in a congressional hearing file.

The disposal is by attribution to circular reporting: 'AARO assesses that the inaccurate claim that the USG is reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology and is hiding it from Congress is, in large part, the result of circular reporting from a group of individuals who believe this to be the case, despite the lack of any evidence.'

_sequence_chain_why: chainHtml() reads s.date, s.event, s.source and s.isAnomalous off every chain step. All 11 sequenceChains on this board held bare node-id strings or free prose instead, so every one rendered an undefined event under an undefined date - on Grusch, Elizondo, Davis and Marcel among others. Nothing threw and no count moved, so nothing caught it. The renderer is inherited from The Vanishing, where a chain step is an ordered, dated, individually sourced link; the research wrote program lineages and shorthand labels into the same field. Each chain below is rebuilt from that person's own on-board chronology, and each step's source is the claim on the same person that covers it. Steps the old chain asserted but the record here does not carry were dropped rather than written from memory. Where no claim on the node covers a step, the source is null and the dock prints 'No attributed source on file', which is the true statement. uap-gerb is set empty: its old chain pointed at Burlison letters that are not on that node, and it has no ordered chain of individually documented links. The dock prints the 'No sequence chain' block, which says that is a finding rather than a gap.
_affiliations_why: affiliations is a PROSE field upstream: The Vanishing writes 'NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (1998-2022)' into it and renders it verbatim. The research on this board wrote node ids into it instead, so 54 entries reached the dossier as raw slugs - a reader saw 'dod-sapco', 'uk-mod-ufo-desk' and 'skidmore-fitts-report' where a name belonged. 46 of them name a real node and the renderer now resolves those to the node's label and makes them navigable, which keeps the link rather than throwing it away. The eight below name an institution that is not on the board, so they are written out as the prose this field has always held, using the name each person's own sub field already gives.
_dates_why: 34 people carried no date. An undated person is invisible to the timeline and to the temporal edge derivation, so the board simply did not connect them. 20 are settled here from the board's own sourced claims. Seven AAWSAP DIRD authors get the exact publication date their own Tier 1 claim states - Towe 31 Mar 2010, Miley 10 Mar 2010, Baker 6 Apr 2010, Leonhardt 2 Mar 2010, Millis 1 Nov 2010, Culbreth 20 Nov 2010, Genik 15 Dec 2010. Thirteen more are DIRD authors whose delivery date this board has not established; they take 2010-01-01, which is the marker already used on Puthoff, Davis and Green for precisely that. It denotes the AAWSAP delivery period and is not a claim about a known day. McKeon and Cole take the seat dates their own claims state. NOT set here: the DIA list date of 9 January 2018 was rejected as a date for these authors. It is when DIA transmitted the title list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, eight years after the work, and using it would place every DIRD author in 2018 and cluster them temporally with the disclosure fight rather than with the programme that commissioned them.
_dates_congress_why: Ten members of the 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) notification group carried no date, so the board could not place them in time at all. Each takes the convening date of the Congress in which that member first held the seat their own sub and Tier 1 claims name - not a date invented for them, and not the date a committee web page was read. Convening dates verified against the Senate's own table: 111th 6 January 2009, 118th 3 January 2023, 119th 3 January 2025. That table is added as a source on each of the ten, because it is what the date rests on.
_dates_researched_why: Two dates could not be derived from the board and were researched. Levy takes 2025-06-01, the publication month of the UAPx field-expedition paper in Progress in Aerospace Sciences 156:101099 - the same date her first author Szydagis already carries on this board for the same paper. Powers takes 2026-05-20, the date the OSD Historical Office's Key Officials list of 7 July 2026 gives for his assumption of the acting Comptroller role. Checking it turned up a live contradiction between two Department pages: the comptroller site's leadership page still names Hurst, while war.gov's biography of Powers says Powers. The Historical Office list dates the handover and settles it, and the contradiction is recorded as a claim rather than quietly resolved.
_dird_label_why: Two distinct DIRDs carried the identical label 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion', so the board showed a reader two nodes it could not tell apart. They are genuinely different documents and both were downloaded and their covers read on 22 August 2026: DIA-08-1011-003 at 50 pages, authored by Culbreth, and DIA-08-1011-004 at 37 pages, authored by Teofilo, both dated 1 November 2010. Both cover pages carry the same title, so the ambiguity is in the source documents, not in this board's transcription of them. The document number is appended to each label because that is what actually distinguishes them and it was read directly off the covers. NOT asserted: which of the two the DIA's 9 January 2018 list calls 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II'. Culbreth's own claim on this board says list item 30 carries that title and is credited to him, which would make DIA-08-1011-003 the 'II' despite the lower document number. The list itself could not be retrieved to check - irp.fas.org returns HTTP 202 with an empty body - so the roman numeral is left off both labels rather than guessed onto one.
